title: One residual companion block with exceptional birth data
statement:
Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a smooth closed pair of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes, $E=(E_1,\ldots,E_t)$ a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary transverse to $N$, $J\subset\mathcal O_N$ coherent and nonzero on every component, and $c\ge1$ an integer [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [pqf-def-coherent]. Here $\operatorname{ord}_x(T)=\sup\{q\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}:T_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, with infinite order for the zero ideal, and $\operatorname{cosupp}(J,c)=\{x:J_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^c\}$. Test sequences use smooth cosupport centers having normal crossings with $E$, controlled transforms for those blowups, and ordinary pullback for line products (adjoining the zero section to the boundary) and exceptional-intersection blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Locally write $J=M R$, where $M=\prod_i\mathcal I_{E_i\cap N}^{a_i}$ has the largest possible nonnegative exponents and $R$ is not divisible by any of these boundary ideals. Put $\mu(x)=\operatorname{ord}_x(R)/c$. For finitely many weighted ideals $(J_i,c_i)$ their marked sum is $(\sum_iJ_i^{L/c_i},L)$ for any positive common multiple $L$ of the marks; changing $L$ gives test-equivalent data.

At a positive maximum $\mu=a/c$ define the companion to be $(R,a)$ if $a\ge c$, and the marked sum $(R,a)+(M,c-a)$ if $0<a<c$. At the birth of a block call all boundary components then present old. Along a history retaining the previous blocks and this block's value, retain their strict transforms as old; components introduced afterwards are new. When the preceding blocks or the positive residual value drop, start this bookkeeping again at the new birth. Let $s(x)$ count the old components through $x$. On a neighbourhood of a point with maximal $(\mu,s)$, augment the companion by the marked ideals $(\mathcal I_{E_i\cap N},1)$ for the old components through that point, and remove those old components from the active boundary for coefficient restriction. In a history produced by these operations and the coefficient restriction of [lem-trf-logarithmic-coefficient-test-equivalence], with each subsequent center in the maximal retained block strata and in the augmented companion's cosupport, the following local assertions hold.

The augmented companion has maximal order (its order equals its mark on cosupport), admits a section of the logarithmic derivative ideal of mark minus one cutting out a smooth maximal-contact hypersurface transverse to the active new boundary, and presents exactly the locus where the retained blocks and the pair $(\mu,s)$ keep their current maximal values. Its cosupport-center blowup sequences identify precisely the original cosupport-center blowup sequences retaining these values; these comparisons persist after each transform. After old components have been encoded as equations, auxiliary exceptional-intersection tests use the common active boundary; line-product tests retain the stated ordinary-pullback convention. The old boundary equations included in the companion ensure that lifted centers have normal crossings with the entire original boundary, including the removed old components.

On the common cosupport (and on the corresponding retained cosupports after transforms), normalized orders $\operatorname{ord}(J)/c$, $\mu$, the normalized exceptional exponents $a_i/c$, and the birth counts are determined by test equivalence between presentations of the same smooth support dimension, with identified ordered boundary histories. Equivalent inputs and choices of local companion or coefficient presentation give equivalent retained-stratum presentations; all these data commute with smooth pullback, including a change of relative dimension. Each single residual-order/birth-count block has finite image on quasi-compact inputs and is upper semicontinuous on the stratum of the preceding blocks. Under a blowup in its represented maximal stratum this pair cannot increase. At a fixed earlier prefix, along all subsequent retained-prefix transforms the positive values of the next residual order lie in $(1/D)\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ for one positive integer $D$ depending on that prefix at its birth, not on the number of later blowups; the birth count cannot increase while that residual order stays fixed. If $\mu=0$ the residual ideal is the unit ideal locally and the remaining marked ideal is exactly the boundary monomial $(M,c)$. These are statements about one block and its companion presentations; they assert neither existence of a full resolution word nor termination.

proof.text: Smoothness gives regular local rings by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. Their boundary parameters are distinct prime elements by [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization]. For finitely many nonzero generators of $J$, take the minimum exponent of each boundary prime and divide every generator by their product. This constructs $M$ and $R$; some divided generator is not divisible by each chosen prime, so the exponents are maximal and the residual ideal is unique up to units. Local generators and their quotients are regular on a sufficiently small neighbourhood; work on its pieces where the relevant boundary components are fixed. The order rules in the differential-calculus lemma give $\operatorname{ord}_xJ=\sum_{E_i\ni x}a_i+\operatorname{ord}_xR$.

proof.text: For a common multiple $L$, the order of $\sum T_i^{L/b_i}$ is $\min_i (L/b_i)\operatorname{ord}T_i$, by the order rules. Thus its cosupport is the intersection of the cosupports of $(T_i,b_i)$. At a common permissible blowup, the smooth center is in each summand's cosupport and has normal crossings with the boundary, so the chart lemma makes every controlled ideal regular and coherent. Thus $e^{-L}\sigma^*(T_i^{L/b_i})=(e^{-b_i}\sigma^*T_i)^{L/b_i}$; ordinary pullback commutes with sums and powers for the two auxiliary operations. Induction on the length of a test sequence proves the same intersection identity after every operation, including equality of permissible centers. Replacing $L$ by a multiple has the same property; two arbitrary choices are compared with their common multiple. This proves the weighted-sum and re-marking convention, rather than assuming it.

proof.text: Shrink around a point of the positive maximum so that $\operatorname{ord}R\le a$. If $a\ge c$, the companion cosupport is $\{\operatorname{ord}R=a\}$, contained in original cosupport. If $0<a<c$, it is $\{\operatorname{ord}R=a,\operatorname{ord}M\ge c-a\}=\{x\in\operatorname{cosupp}(J,c):\mu(x)=a/c\}$. At every such point the residual summand has order exactly its mark $a$. Consequently its $L/a$th power has order $L$ and the other summands have order at least $L$; the marked sum has order exactly $L$. Adding old-boundary ideals of mark one preserves this equality on the resulting intersection. The argument uses the minimum rule, so no cancellation of leading terms is being assumed.

proof.text: For a center in this cosupport, apply [lem-trf-equimultiple-weak-transform-order] to $(R,a)$ and [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts] to $(J,c)$. Here $J$ and $R$ are nonzero on every component and both have positive marks; a center cannot contain a whole component, since its generic local ring is a field. The chart lemma preserves smooth support, boundary and componentwise nonvanishing. In a chart with exceptional equation $e$, put $R'=e^{-a}\sigma^*R$ and $M'=e^{a-c}\sigma^*M$. Then $J'=M'R'$. If $v=\operatorname{ord}_T M$ is the sum of exponents of the boundary components containing the center, the exceptional exponent of $M'$ is $v+a-c\ge0$: this is automatic for $a\ge c$, and for $a<c$ follows from the center's membership in $(M,c-a)$. The weak-transform lemma gives $\operatorname{ord}R'\le a$ and no exceptional factor. Surviving old boundary factors are absent from $R'$ too. Thus this is exactly the refactorization at the next stage, and $\mu'\le a/c$. For $a<c$, $M'$ is precisely the transform of $(M,c-a)$; for $a\ge c$ only $(R,a)$ is needed in the companion. In either case the companion's cosupport is the original transformed cosupport with residual order still $a/c$.

proof.text: Fix the birth stage while the preceding blocks and $\mu$ remain fixed. Through a point with maximum old count $s$, shrink to exclude every old component not through that point. There are then at most $s$ old components on this neighbourhood; the equality $s(x)=s$ means that all their equations vanish. Step 2 shows that adjoining those equations with mark one represents precisely this locus. A subsequent center lies in every one of these old components. In the adapted charts of the chart lemma an old equation is a center coordinate $u_j$: it becomes $e(u_j/e)$ when $j$ is not the pivot. Dividing by $e$ at mark one leaves its strict-transform equation; at the pivot it leaves $1$. This uses the general coordinate charts, even if the center has additional nonboundary equations. An old component absent from a chart gives a unit equation and hence empty augmented cosupport there. Old components never acquire a new label: at every point above the center the old components present form a subset of those at its image. Hence $s$ cannot increase while $\mu$ stays fixed. If $\mu$ or an earlier block drops, take the new birth stipulated in the statement; a drop of $s$ alone retains the previous birth list.

proof.text: At birth the active boundary is empty, since all its components were declared old. Apply the differential-calculus lemma first to the residual summand $(R,a)$: its maximum order is $a$, so a derivative of order $a-1$ gives a smooth contact hypersurface. Carry this contact equation through the retained history. The same lemma keeps its transforms logarithmic, of order one, and transverse to the active new boundary. It also gives contact for the augmented ideal, whose mark is $d$: in the coordinate directions tangent to all active boundary equations, choose $v$ and a residual generator $f$ with $\partial_v^a f$ nonzero at the point. Such a free direction exists because the residual contact equation has a nonzero free linear term. The degree-$d$ Taylor coefficient of $f^{d/a}$ in a suitable free direction is nonzero. Its derivative of order $d-1$ has a nonzero free linear term, lies in the logarithmic derivative ideal of the augmented sum, and cuts out a hypersurface transverse to the active boundary. Apply differential-transform inclusion to this equation along each fixed augmented presentation. When $s$ drops at fixed $\mu$, repeat the free-direction argument for the newly augmented sum using the already transported residual contact. Characteristic zero is used to differentiate the powers. This establishes contact after every re-augmentation without declaring new components old prematurely.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-logarithmic-coefficient-test-equivalence] to this augmented ideal with active boundary only. Step 6 checks both hypotheses: order at most the mark near cosupport, and an order-one logarithmic derivative defining a hypersurface transverse to that boundary. The coefficient presentation on that hypersurface has the same test sequences in the common ambient scheme, including transformed cosupports; its mark can be fixed to $d!$. A lifted smooth center lies in all the encoded old hypersurfaces and has normal crossings with the active ones. To check the full boundary condition, first take the smooth intersection of those old coordinate hypersurfaces. The center is smooth inside it; the active hypersurfaces containing the center provide independent further conormal coordinates, and the remaining active ones restrict to coordinate hypersurfaces on the center by its normal-crossings condition. Complete these coordinates along the smooth closed pair using [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates]. This makes the center a coordinate subspace and every original boundary component a coordinate hyperplane. Thus removing the old components from the active list has lost no boundary condition.

proof.text: Induct on a retained history. Initially Steps 3 and 5 identify augmented cosupport with the fixed $(\mu,s)$ stratum inside the earlier retained stratum. For a cosupport blowup, Steps 4 and 5 identify the next cosupport and next permissible centers in both directions. A line product preserves the equations and adds a new, not old, component. Consider the blowup $\sigma$ of $W=H_1\cap H_2\cap N$ for two active boundary components, with new exceptional divisor $F$; a test transformation of $(R,a)$; $R$, $M$ pull back ordinarily. Suppose $\sigma^*R$ is divisible by the equation of $F$ near a point $x'$ over $W$, so $R$ vanishes along $W$. Derivations preserving $\mathcal I_{H_1}$ and $\mathcal I_{H_2}$ preserve their sum, so every logarithmic derivative of $R$, in particular the transported residual contact equation $h$, vanishes along $W$, and $\sigma^*h$ is divisible by the equation of $F$. If moreover $\operatorname{ord}_{x'}\sigma^*R\ge a$, then $x'$ lies in the transformed cosupport of $(R,a)$, and the differential-calculus lemma, applied to this test sequence, says that near $x'$ the pullback $\sigma^*h$ has order one and $V(\sigma^*h)$ is transverse to the transformed active boundary, which contains $F$; but a smooth hypersurface containing $F$ equals $F$ near $x'$, a contradiction. If instead $\operatorname{ord}_{x'}\sigma^*R<a$, then $x'$ lies neither in the pulled-back companion cosupport nor in the retained stratum, since the true residual divides $\sigma^*R$ and has order at most $\operatorname{ord}_{x'}\sigma^*R<a$. Thus on both loci ordinary pullback creates no residual exceptional factor, and the same numerical conditions describe the retained cosupport after this operation. The coefficient lemma preserves the induction through coefficient restriction. Auxiliary exceptional tests use the common active boundary; cosupport-center blowups are compared in both directions with the full original boundary.

proof.text: On common cosupport, [lem-trf-test-sequence-order-recovery] recovers $\operatorname{ord}J/c$ and each $a_i/c$ from equivalent data of the same support dimension. Their difference $\operatorname{ord}J/c-\sum_{E_i\ni x}a_i/c$ is $\mu(x)$ by Step 1. Apply this after each common sequence. Equality of the preceding block values and $\mu$ identifies their first drop and their birth stages; with identified ordered boundary histories the subsets of old labels therefore coincide, and so do their counts. This is an induction on the finite history, starting with the same birth list; it does not assume numerical invariance away from cosupport.

proof.text: To compare companions, initially their normalized monomial divisors $M^{1/c}$ and residual marks $a/c$ agree by Step 9. Along any common companion test sequence track the monomial factor with mark $c-a$ (formally allowing a nonpositive mark when $a\ge c$): at a cosupport blowup its exceptional exponent divided by $c$ is $\sum a_i/c+a/c-1$, and at an auxiliary operation it is ordinary pullback. These formulas agree for equivalent inputs. At a point of original transformed cosupport, subtract its tracked monomial order from the recovered $\operatorname{ord}J_t/c$. Companion cosupport means that the result is at least the fixed $a/c$ and, when $a<c$, that the tracked monomial order is at least $1-a/c$. Thus both presentations have the same next cosupport and permissible centers. Step 2 adds identical old equations; induction proves equivalence of augmented companions, not just equality of their initial sets. Finally apply the choice-independence assertion of [lem-trf-logarithmic-coefficient-test-equivalence] for coefficient equations and coordinates. The same argument applies at every lower support dimension, comparing presentations of that same dimension.

proof.text: Under smooth pullback the order function and logarithmic differential ideals pull back by the differential-calculus lemma. Divisorial exponents are unchanged, computed at the generic points of the pulled-back smooth boundary components; absence of a boundary factor in $R$ is preserved there as well. Sums, powers, old equations and their ordered birth labels therefore pull back. The chart lemma applies to the pulled-back smooth closed pair and smooth cosupport center with its pulled-back normal-crossings coordinates; it identifies the pulled-back strict support with its blowup, preserves the ordered boundary, and identifies the controlled ideal formulas under smooth base change, and the coefficient lemma gives compatibility of restriction and its comparisons. These are statements at a point of any smooth pullback, with no fixed relative dimension: extra free coordinates contribute no generators of the pulled-back ideal. Hence each construction and the retained test comparisons commute with arbitrary smooth pullback.

proof.text: Induct on the finite history for upper semicontinuity. At the current stage the residual ideal is coherent and nonzero on every smooth component. Its order has finite image on quasi-compact opens and closed upper-level sets by the differential-calculus lemma. A finite cover by factorization charts bounds all orders. At a fixed preceding prefix the mark is fixed, so $\mu$ has finite image and is upper semicontinuous. On a current residual-value stratum $\mu=r$, each earlier residual value, pulled back along the history, is upper semicontinuous by the induction hypothesis and at least $r$ by nonincrease. Partition this stratum by the first stage $b$ at which the value equals $r$. The condition that it is greater than $r$ at each earlier stage is closed, because the earlier functions have finite image. Hence the closure of a birth-$b$ piece can enter only the same or a later birth piece. A later birth declares a superset of the surviving earlier-born boundary labels old. For any subset $A$ of $k$ old labels at birth $b$, intersect its birth piece with their $k$ closed hypersurfaces at the current stage. Every closure point still lies on those hypersurfaces and its birth is no earlier, so these $k$ labels are still old there. There are finitely many stages and label subsets. The union of these pieces is $\{s\ge k\}$, and the closure calculation proves it is closed in $\mu=r$. This proves finite image and upper semicontinuity of the pair on the preceding-prefix stratum, starting with the fixed initial birth. Step 4 proves nonincrease of $\mu$ under a represented maximum blowup; Step 5 proves nonincrease of $s$ when $\mu$ is unchanged.

proof.text: Fix an earlier prefix at its birth and keep one integral marked presentation of it. On its fixed smooth support, controlled transforms never change its mark. If a lower support is required, form each companion weighted sum with one fixed common multiple of its integer marks, then use the coefficient mark $d!$. With the earlier residual values fixed their numerators and these marks are fixed, recursively from the first mark; adjoining old equations of mark one does not change the chosen common multiple. Consequently the next support has a single fixed integer mark $c_*$ throughout every retained-prefix sequence. Its next residual orders are integers divided by $c_*$, even when that next value drops and the old bookkeeping restarts. Take $D=c_*$, or the least common multiple of the finitely many chart marks at birth. Equivalent re-markings do not alter the rational values by Step 9. Thus $D$ is chosen at birth and does not accumulate factors from later blowups. This proves bounded denominators without inferring it from mere rationality.

proof.text: If $\mu(x)=0$, then $R_x$ is not contained in the maximal ideal, so it contains a unit and equals $\mathcal O_{N,x}$. Coherence permits shrinking so that a chosen unit generator remains invertible; hence $R=\mathcal O_N$ there and $J=M$. This includes the empty and unit-cosupport cases. No termination assertion or full resolution word has been used.

statement_correction.old_statement:
Let $N\hookrightarrow Z$ be a smooth closed pair of finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes, $E=(E_1,\ldots,E_t)$ a finite ordered simple normal crossings boundary transverse to $N$, $J\subset\mathcal O_N$ coherent and nonzero on every component, and $c\ge1$ an integer [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [pqf-def-coherent]. Here $\operatorname{ord}_x(T)=\sup\{q\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}:T_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^q\}$, with infinite order for the zero ideal, and $\operatorname{cosupp}(J,c)=\{x:J_x\subseteq\mathfrak m_x^c\}$. Test sequences use smooth cosupport centers having normal crossings with $E$, controlled transforms for those blowups, and ordinary pullback for line products (adjoining the zero section to the boundary) and exceptional-intersection blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Locally write $J=M R$, where $M=\prod_i\mathcal I_{E_i\cap N}^{a_i}$ has the largest possible nonnegative exponents and $R$ is not divisible by any of these boundary ideals. Put $\mu(x)=\operatorname{ord}_x(R)/c$. For finitely many weighted ideals $(J_i,c_i)$ their marked sum is $(\sum_iJ_i^{L/c_i},L)$ for any positive common multiple $L$ of the marks; changing $L$ gives test-equivalent data.

At a positive maximum $\mu=a/c$ define the companion to be $(R,a)$ if $a\ge c$, and the marked sum $(R,a)+(M,c-a)$ if $0<a<c$. At the birth of a block call all boundary components then present old. Along a history retaining the previous blocks and this block's value, retain their strict transforms as old; components introduced afterwards are new. When the preceding blocks or the positive residual value drop, start this bookkeeping again at the new birth. Let $s(x)$ count the old components through $x$. On a neighbourhood of a point with maximal $(\mu,s)$, augment the companion by the marked ideals $(\mathcal I_{E_i\cap N},1)$ for the old components through that point, and remove those old components from the active boundary for coefficient restriction. In a history produced by these operations and the coefficient restriction of [lem-trf-logarithmic-coefficient-test-equivalence], with each subsequent center in the maximal retained block strata and in the augmented companion's cosupport, the following local assertions hold.

The augmented companion has maximal order (its order equals its mark on cosupport), admits a section of the logarithmic derivative ideal of mark minus one cutting out a smooth maximal-contact hypersurface transverse to the active new boundary, and presents exactly the locus where the retained blocks and the pair $(\mu,s)$ keep their current maximal values. Its cosupport-center test sequences identify precisely the original test sequences retaining these values; these comparisons persist after each transform. The old boundary equations included in the companion ensure that lifted centers have normal crossings with the entire original boundary, including the removed old components.

Normalized orders $\operatorname{ord}(J)/c$, $\mu$, the normalized exceptional exponents $a_i/c$, and the birth counts are determined by test equivalence between presentations of the same smooth support dimension, with identified ordered boundary histories. Equivalent inputs and choices of local companion or coefficient presentation give equivalent retained-stratum presentations; all these data commute with smooth pullback, including a change of relative dimension. Each single residual-order/birth-count block has finite image on quasi-compact inputs and is upper semicontinuous on the stratum of the preceding blocks. Under a blowup in its represented maximal stratum this pair cannot increase. At a fixed earlier prefix, along all subsequent retained-prefix transforms the positive values of the next residual order lie in $(1/D)\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$ for one positive integer $D$ depending on that prefix at its birth, not on the number of later blowups; the birth count cannot increase while that residual order stays fixed. If $\mu=0$ the residual ideal is the unit ideal locally and the remaining marked ideal is exactly the boundary monomial $(M,c)$. These are statements about one block and its companion presentations; they assert neither existence of a full resolution word nor termination.
